title: Childhood schooling and plantation work
summary: He learned to read on his own; his father was a tenant farmer working sunrise to sundown.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That time in Europe, too, I think broadened you. Huh? I think that time in Europe broadened you over what would have happened here in America. Well. In interest.
Because you had contact with these people.

I had contact with them, but this thing of continuing reading, that came from me because I just walked a mile, a mile and a half, going to learn my ABCs because my father couldn't send me to school at that time.
You know, he was working from Kent to Kent and the end of the year just paying his chemics of debts and start over. Where was your mom? In Louisiana.

Oh. Northern New York. Northern New York. Well, it's south west. Oh, way over at the... Yeah. Spider-Golf in Mexico. That came to Kent, that has a lot of meaning in the Nicholas music, doesn't it? Yes, because it means from sunrise to sundown. And boy, there's no blues more miserable than knowing that you're going to have to wake up to face that. Again. There's your blues.

And the head man, he's home. He have his boy that's going to ring the bell when the sun... Yeah. And he better be up and ring the bell so the whole vacation... And you can experience a bit of joy when it's over. At the evening. And he can get up and see, you ring that bell and you ring it hard so every... all the farmers know he has to get up and the sun is rising by the time you can see. Yeah. But in the wintertime during Truby Cain's season, you don't wait for the sun to rise. You've got to be there when you can see that stick going and going of Cain and going away until you can't see no more. Oh, that's seven days a week. Frank, no Sunday.
